processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Owing to the number of Warwick County court records taken during the Civil War, a significant portion of these records were acquired piecemeal over decades through donations from individuals of both original materials and reproductions. Transfers of original surviving records from the Circuit Court Clerk duplicated some of the previously acquired reproductions. In 2014, many of the original records were digitized as part of the Lost Records Localities Digital Collection. Consequently, in October 2025, it was decided to deaccession reproductions for which both the original and a digitized copy existed. Reproductions were maintained (BC#7417689) for those records not held in original form.

Due to the scarcity of pre-1865 original Warwick County court records, as well as the incomplete nature of many donated records, the pre-1865 materials have been organized under the heading "Records." Individial documents have been foldered and labeled, but have not been organized into established local records series at this time. Box lists for the records in Series I: Processed Records has been provided. Post-1865 records have been organized under local records series.
Encoded by C. Freed: September 2020; updated by V. Brooks: October 2025.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: Locality History: Warwick County (extinct) was named for Robert Rich, earl of Warwick, a prominent member of the London Company, or for the county of Warwick in England. The county was originally called Warwick River and was one of the original shires, or counties, first enumerated in 1634. The name was shortened to Warwick in 1643. Warwick County became extinct in 1952, when it became the city of Warwick. The new city was consolidated with the city of Newport News in 1958 and took the latter's name.

Newport News probably commemorated Christopher Newport, who made five voyages to Virginia between 1607 and 1619. The Old Dominion Land Company bought land there in 1880 and began laying out a new village in October. Newport News was incorporated as a city by Act of the General Assembly in 1896 without ever having been incorporated as a town. On 1 July 1958 Newport News was enlarged by consolidating with the City of Warwick, which then became extinct. In the years before consolidation, Newport News annexed land from Warwick County in 1917, 1921 and 1940; from Elizabeth City County in 1927 and 1937; and from both Elizabeth City County and Warwick counties in 1921.

Warwick County court records were destroyed several times, with most destruction occuring during the Civil War. The clerk's office was burned on 15 December 1864. County court minute books and loose records from 1787 to 1819 were destroyed by this fire. Additiona records were burned on 3 April 1865, in Richmond, where the county records had been moved for safekeeping during the Civil War.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Newport News/Warwick County (Va.) Records, 1646-1971, consist of the following series: County and City Court Records (subfield series include Judgments, Clerk' Records, Jury Records, Common Law papers and Chancery Records, Election Records, Fiduciary Records, Bonds/Commissions/Oaths, County Administrative Records (subfield series include Board of Supervisors Records and Board of Supervisors Records: Road and Bridge Records), Tax and Fiscal Records, Business Records, Organization Records, Fiduciary Records, Wills, Military and Pension Records, Miscellaneous Records and Property Records.
Many of the surviving pre-1866 Warwick County records are incomplete, damaged, or fragments. This includes materials originally part of volumes, as well as loose papers.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Material
relatedmaterial.p: Additional Newport News and Warwick County Records can be found on microfilm at the Library of Virginia. Consult "A Guide to Virginia County and City Records on Microfilm" found on the Library of Virginia's web site.

Warwick County is one of Virginia's Lost Records Localities. Additional Warwick County Records may be found in the Virginia Lost Records Localities Collection at the Library of Virginia. Search the Lost Records Localities Digital Collection.

scopecontent.p: This series contains both original and reproduction copies of Warwick County records. A significant number of these records are partial or damaged.
